name: Pacific Biosciences of Californ
business_overview: Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. designs, develops, and manufactures sequencing solutions to resolve genetically complex problems. The company provides sequencing systems; consumable products, including single molecule real-time (SMRT) technology; long-read sequencing; and various reagent kits designed for specific workflow, such as preparation kit to convert DNA into SMRTbell double-stranded DNA library formats, including molecular biology reagents, such as ligase, buffers, and exonucleases. It also offers binding kits, such as modified DNA polymerase used to bind SMRTbell libraries to the polymerase in preparation for sequencing; and sequencing kits comprise reagents required for on-instrument, real-time sequencing, including the phospholinked nucleotides. In addition, the company provides Revio, Vega, and Sequel instruments which conduct, monitor, and analyze single-molecule biochemical reactions on SMRT cell microchips; short-read sequencing; and onso instrument. It serves academic and governmental research institutions, commercial testing and service laboratories, genome centers, public health labs, hospitals and clinical research institutes, contract research organizations, pharmaceutical companies, and agricultural companies. The company markets its products through a sales force and distribution partners in Australia, certain parts of Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Central America, and South America. It has a collaboration with DNAstack Inc. to provide federated dataset of HiFi whole genome sequencing data. The company was formerly known as Nanofluidics, Inc. and changed its name to Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. in 2005. Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. was incorporated in 2000 and is headquartered in Menlo Park, California.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Designs and manufactures sequencing instruments and consumables for genomic research.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** A demand shift is underway, with record consumables driven by surging clinical-adoption and higher utilization, while instrument revenue lags under sustained academic and government funding pressure in the U.S. and competitive ASP compression, particularly for Vega. Geographic divergence is pronounced: EMEA consumables demand is expanding, Americas are subdued, and Asia‑Pacific is declining. Large-scale collaborations (Basecamp Research’s Trillion Gene Atlas for AI development, DNAstack’s federated whole-genome dataset) underscore the platform’s relevance, and the SPRQ‑Nx beta expansion signals upcoming product momentum, but near‑term instrument softness tempers the top‑line story.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership is tightly managing costs—operating expenses fell significantly, the non‑GAAP loss narrowed, and an IP sale to Illumina bolstered the cash cushion—while steering the portfolio toward higher‑growth clinical consumables and strategic partnerships. The Vega rollout disappointed versus internal expectations, and a one‑time promotion weighed on gross margin alongside elevated compute costs, but the rapid build‑out of the SPRQ‑Nx commercial launch and the Basecamp deal reflect deliberate positioning for a sequencing‑driven AI opportunity. Overall, execution is mixed: clinical traction and expense discipline are building credibility, yet instrument underperformance and missed revenue guidance highlight ongoing headwinds.

Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. PACB, popularly known as PacBio, delivered an adjusted loss per share of 12 cents in first-quarter 2026, narrower than the year-ago adjusted loss of 15 cents per share. The adjusted loss per share topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 29.4%.

The company’s GAAP loss per share was 3 cents in the quarter compared with the year-ago period’s loss of $1.44.

PacBio registered total revenues of $37.2 million in the first quarter, flat year over year. The figure missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 9.3%.
